meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
You're clearly a brilliant lawyer, and I really respect how hard you fight for Owen.
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Can you step out of the role and tell me how I should handle this?
You want me to tell you how to handle your own meeting? Take the zero off, Hale. Then tell me who decided it and when.
I just want us to be on the same team here.
Then why are we here? A teammate would have picked up the phone before entering a zero. Who decided, Hale?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want Owen's zero withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone contacted me, and a plain answer on who decided it and whether Owen was heard first. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an answer on who decided and whether Owen was heard first.
What moved her: nothing, because none of your turns gave her a fact or a document to weigh.
What cost ground: asking her to tell you how to handle the meeting, because it handed her control and lowered her respect for you, with the praise and the same-team appeal adding to it because she reads them as being managed.
Try next time: on your first turn, instead of praising her, say in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called her, then answer her question about who decided and when.
